q: A solution is a homogeneous (uniform) mixture of two or more ____.
e: A solution is a homogeneous (uniform) mixture of two or more substances. A mixture holds substances together physically, and its composition can vary.

q: The ocean is a vast water solution containing different compounds extracted from the minerals of the Earth's ____.
e: The ocean is a vast water solution containing different compounds extracted from the minerals of the Earth's crust. Crust is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Sugar is the solute, and water is the .
e: Sugar is the solute, and water is the. The solvent is the liquid that does the dissolving, often water.

q: Some liquids can mix with one another in all proportions ( liquids), while some liquids do not mix (immiscible liquids).
e: Some liquids can mix with one another in all proportions (liquids), while some liquids do not mix (immiscible liquids). Miscible is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Solutions may be gaseous, solid, or ____ in nature.
e: Solutions may be gaseous, solid, or liquid in nature. Liquid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Dry air is a familiar example of a ____ solution.
e: Dry air is a familiar example of a gaseous solution. Gaseous is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Brass (copper and zinc) is an example of a ____ solution.
e: Brass (copper and zinc) is an example of a solid solution. Solid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Solutions having water as the solvent are referred to as ____ solutions.
e: Solutions having water as the solvent are referred to as aqueous solutions. Aqueous is the idea that completes this fact.

q: If some more solid added can dissolve with stirring, this solution is known as an ____ solution.
e: If some more solid added can dissolve with stirring, this solution is known as an unsaturated solution. Unsaturated is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A ____ solution forms when no more solute can be dissolved in the given amount of solvent at that temperature even if it is stirred.
e: A saturated solution forms when no more solute can be dissolved in the given amount of solvent at that temperature even if it is stirred. Saturated is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The amount (in grams) of the solute in 100 g of water to give a saturated solution at that experimental temperature is known as the ____ of that solute.
e: The amount (in grams) of the solute in 100 g of water to give a saturated solution at that experimental temperature is known as the solubility of that solute. Solubility is the idea that completes this fact.

q: If the solution contains more solute than it should have at room temperature, it is a ____ solution.
e: If the solution contains more solute than it should have at room temperature, it is a supersaturated solution. Supersaturated is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Solubility of the solute depends, in part, on the temperature of the ____.
e: Solubility of the solute depends, in part, on the temperature of the solvent. The solvent is the liquid that does the dissolving, often water.

q: When the temperature of the solution is increased the solubility of the solute ____.
e: When the temperature of the solution is increased the solubility of the solute increases. Increases is the idea that completes this fact.

q: There are some exceptions, such as the solubility of all gases and some solids like calcium hydroxide and calcium sulphate, which decreases when temperature of the solution is ____.
e: There are some exceptions, such as the solubility of all gases and some solids like calcium hydroxide and calcium sulphate, which decreases when temperature of the solution is increased. Increased is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When a saturated solution at a higher temperature is cooled, the solubility ____.
e: When a saturated solution at a higher temperature is cooled, the solubility decreases. Decreases is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A solute is a substance which dissolves in a solvent to give a ____.
e: A solute is a substance which dissolves in a solvent to give a solution. A solution is a homogeneous mixture of solute dissolved in solvent.

q: A solvent is a substance, mostly liquid, in which another substance dissolves to give a ____ mixture.
e: A solvent is a substance, mostly liquid, in which another substance dissolves to give a homogeneous mixture. A homogeneous mixture looks the same throughout, like a clear solution.

q: Solubility of a substance at a given temperature is the mass in grams of the substance which will saturate ____ g of water, at that temperature.
e: Solubility of a substance at a given temperature is the mass in grams of the substance which will saturate 100 g of water, at that temperature. 100 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Matter is everything that we come across in our lives, like the air you breathe, the clothes you wear and the water you ____.
e: Matter is everything that we come across in our lives, like the air you breathe, the clothes you wear and the water you drink. Drink is the idea that completes this fact.

q: An element is a substance that cannot be broken down into other simpler substances through ____ means.
e: An element is a substance that cannot be broken down into other simpler substances through chemical means. Chemical is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A compound is a substance containing two or more different elements chemically joined together in a fixed ____.
e: A compound is a substance containing two or more different elements chemically joined together in a fixed ratio. Ratio is the idea that completes this fact.
